content: The Dipsacales are an order of flowering plants that belong to the asterid group within the dicotyledons. According to the Cronquist system of classification, this order traditionally included the families Adoxaceae, Caprifoliaceae, Dipsacaceae, and Valerianaceae. However, under the more recent Angiosperm Phylogeny Group (APG II) system, the composition of the order remains largely similar, but the families are defined differently. In the APG system, the order includes the family Adoxaceae and a broadly defined Caprifoliaceae. The latter encompasses several families that were previously recognized as separate, such as Diervillaceae, Dipsacaceae, Linnaeaceae, Morinaceae, and Valerianaceae. Under the APG II classification, some well-known members of the Dipsacales order include honeysuckle, elder, viburnum, and valerian. Additionally, a few other families may be closely related to this order. These include the Columelliaceae, Paracryphiaceae, and Sphenostemonaceae families.
